newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU COMMISSION HINTS AT ANTI-PVC MEASURES.
newsitem.headline: EU COMMISSION HINTS AT ANTI-PVC MEASURES.

text.p: The European Commission hinted on Wednesday at future EU measures to limit the use of polyvinyl chloride (PVC), saying it would study the plastic and the pollutants released during its incineration.

"The Commission will consider the scientific evidence concerning PVC and, if necessary, will make appropriate proposals to take such evidence into account," it said in the summary of a proposal intended to limit the waste generated by scrapped cars.

"This (is) because the disposal of PVC through incineration, both with and without energy recovery, poses major problems," it said, adding that the plastic had lower calorific values when burnt and generated toxic waste products which increased the cost of scrubbing flue gases of those pollutants.
"The subsitution of PVC with other materials (in cars) is technically possible but at a higher cost, which varies between 25 and 100 European currency units," it said.
A Commission statement accompanying the proposal announced plans to tackle PVC problems "horizontally" rather than purely in relation to cars, suggesting a wider-ranging action.
An official refused to give any more details of plans.
